name: Minimum Vertex Cover
problem_statement: Find a smallest set of vertices touching every edge, or decide whether a cover of size at most k exists.

normalization: Preserve external vertex identities and isolated vertices.
Reject self-loops and collapse parallel edges only under the declared aggregation rule.

problem_inputs.name: mode
problem_inputs.description: Optimization, parameterized decision, or heuristic feasible cover.

problem_inputs.name: k
problem_inputs.description: Nonnegative bound required for decision mode; otherwise ignored.

required_outputs.name: cover
required_outputs.description: Feasible cover witness when available; null if no witness is returned.

required_outputs.name: cover_size
required_outputs.description: Cardinality of a witness or the optimum size from a size-only solver.

required_outputs.name: decision
required_outputs.description: True or false only if the bounded decision is established; otherwise null.

required_outputs.name: termination_reason
required_outputs.description: Exhausted search, timeout, heuristic completion, or other reason.

solution_semantics.objective: Find a smallest set of vertices touching every edge, or decide whether a cover of size at most k exists.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mathematical objective; implementations must declare approximation and termination status.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each external vertex ID occurs once; output multiplicities follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No ordering among equally valid solutions is required.

validation_rules: For a returned witness, verify that every edge has at least one endpoint in the cover.
Validate optimum sizes and bounded decisions by exhaustive search on small graphs.
Timeout without a witness is unknown, not proof that no cover exists.
A size-only solver must declare that it did not return a witness.
The complement of a cover is independent, but maximality alone does not establish minimum cover size.
edge_cases: Edgeless graphs have an empty optimum cover.
k=0 is feasible exactly for an edgeless graph.
